verdict.reasoning: Patient reports a left-sided headache starting at mid-day and worsening with movement of head/neck: 'terrible headache since mid-day... on the left side' and 'if I lean forward, or like move my head or neck, yeah, headache gets worse.' She also describes it as 'throbbing... on that left side.'

Patient describes visual aura and bilateral blurring before pain: 'I noticed some zig-zag lines in my vision a few minutes before the headache started' and later confirms 'Both eyes, OK' when asked if the blurred vision was in both eyes.
Nausea/vomiting and photophobia without fever are documented: 'I just feel like I need to vomit' and 'I vomited twice'; 'the light's really hurting my eyes'; and 'no I don't feel feverish.'

Second similar episode this month, lasting a couple of days and helped by analgesia and rest: 'I did have a similar headache a few weeks ago' and 'How long did it last for? Patient: Couple of days.' and 'I had to take painkillers, and had to go go to bed and rest.' Doctor later summarizes: 'this is the second migraine you've had in the space of a month.'

Patient denies focal neurological symptoms, trauma, and breathlessness: 'Have you noticed any problems with your speech at all... ? Patient: No.'; 'Any problems with your arms and legs? ... numbness or weakness? Patient: No.'; 'Any difficulty with balance... ? Patient: No.'; 'Have you had a fall recently, or been knocked on the head? Patient: No.'; 'your breathing's OK? You're not feeling breathless... ?' (no concern raised).
Patient reports no past medical problems: 'Do you have any other medical history I should be aware of? Patient: No, nothing.'
Family history includes migraines and underactive thyroid in mother: 'My mum, my mum has, has migraines.' and 'My mom has an underactive thyroid as well.'
Use of Microgynon for 3 months is stated: 'Um I take the pill, Microgynon.' and 'How long have you been on that for? Patient: three months.'

Social history matches: 'I work in the fashion industry' and 'it's really stressful, actually' with managers putting pressure; 'I live on my own'; and 'Do you smoke at all? and do you drink much in the way of alcohol? Patient: No. Patient: No.'

Doctor assesses migraine-type headache, second episode within a month, with aura features: 'I wonder whether you may, uh may have a migraine, uh migraine type headache' and 'this is the second migraine you've had in the space of a month.' Visual aura with zig-zag lines supports 'migraine with aura'; this is the first documented consultation for migraine despite prior similar episode.

Health anxiety about brain cancer is clearly expressed: 'I'm just really worried... it could be a sign of brain cancer.' and 'My, my friend's mum... recently died of a brain tumor. So, it's really concerning me actually.' and 'I was so worried that I had cancer.'

Transcript shows job is 'really stressful' with pressure from managers, but it is not explicitly linked as a contributor to the headache: no direct statement that occupational stress is contributing to her current symptoms.

Doctor advises analgesics including paracetamol/co-codamol and NSAIDs: 'some strong painkillers would be advisable. So, think about Paracetamol, or even Co-codamol. Um, and some anti-inflammatories, such as Ibuprofen and Naproxen.' Use of 'with or without' is consistent with offered options.
Advice to rest in a dark quiet room and stay hydrated is not mentioned in the transcript; only medications, diary, prophylaxis, and safety-netting are discussed.
Keeping a headache diary is explicitly advised: 'I think keeping a headache diary would be quite important, uh to see exactly what's triggering these headaches.'

Doctor advises return if not getting better in 2–3 days, or if worsening headache, neck pain, weakness, or vision issues, but does not mention 'increased frequency' nor 'persistence for more than 2–3 days' as criteria: 'if your symptoms aren't getting better next two three days, or indeed they're getting worse... if your headache's getting worse... or you develop any weakness in your arms and legs, or your vision, then I want you to come back.' The added criterion of increased frequency is not in the transcript.

Follow-up and possible prophylaxis are discussed: 'then we could have a discussion next time I see you next week, perhaps.' and 'we could maybe think about giving you some medications that will stop your headaches from happening in the first place, something prophylactic medicines.'
There is no explicit plan in the transcript to discuss the relationship between oral contraceptive pills and migraine at the next review; OCP is only noted as current medication for contraception.

Doctor reassures about low likelihood of brain cancer but does not explicitly provide formal stress-management support. Reassurance is clear: 'I'm reassured that you don't have anything more serious, such as meningitis, or indeed Brain cancer, I know that was a big worry of yours initially.' and 'I hope that puts your... mind at ease.' However, 'offer support for stress management' is not documented, making that portion an ADDITION. Overall, because the fact combines a supported and an added element, it is best classified as ADDITION.
